steps.text: Melt chocolate over a double boiler or in the microwave, stirring occasionally until smooth. Sift together flour, cocoa, baking powder, and salt; set aside.

In a medium bowl, cream butter with white sugar and brown sugar until smooth. Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in coffee crystals and vanilla until well blended. Stir in melted chocolate. Using a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients just until everything comes together. Cover, and let stand for 35 minutes so the chocolate can set up.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line two cookie sheets with parchment paper.
Roll dough into walnut-sized balls, or drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets, leaving 2 inches between cookies.

Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven. Cookies will be set, but the centers will still be very soft because of the chocolate. Allow cookies to cool on the baking sheets for 10 minutes before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Ultimate Double Chocolate Cookies
raw_recipe.description: The ultimate chocolate chocolate chip cookies with the intensity of hot fudge sauce. So chocolaty we say it twice. This is the best cookie, thick and chewy!

review.reviewBody: I never had a chance to find out how long these cookies were supposed to "set" on the cookie sheets because they all disappeared long before the 10 minutes were up! A few substitutions I made because I was working with a pretty basic food supply: 2 2/3 cups chocolate chips is about a pound of semisweet chocolate; add 1/4 tsp baking soda to regular cocoa powder if you can't get "Dutch process"; if you use salted butter, reduce salt by 1/2 amount. Do use parchment paper, but otherwise there is nothing tricky or difficult or fussy about these cookies. I had requests for another batch before I had finished washing up from the first one!

I didn’t have any problems stirring this like some people did, but to be fair I used a kitchen aid with the paddle attachment. If you’re having trouble mixing the melted chocolate, you likely either didn’t melt the chocolate enough or you burned it (if it looks like it’s crystallizing you cooked it too much). I also waited to melt mine in the microwave until after I mixed the dry ingredients. I made mine into more of a Mexican hot chocolate flavor by adding 1 tsp cinnamon powder, 1/8 tsp cayenne powder, and 1/8 tsp red chili powder to a half-batch of dough (sift in with the other dry ingredients). It’s got some heat so be prepared and experiment until you find a ratio that works for you.

These are the best chocolate cookies ever, so nice and crispy. I made them for a cookie exchange and now making them again to gift family for Christmas. I used 2 2/3 C of chocolate chips as another reviewer suggested as well as .634 C of butter for the 10 TBSP. I had salted butter so decreased the salt to 1/2 tsp. They are a bit sticky rolling balls..I also pressed them with my palm. They do spread so leave enough space between them. Roll no bigger than the walnut sized balls.. come out perfectly round and pretty to gift.

Rich and chocolatey! I read another review that suggested reducing salt to 1/2 tsp. if using salted butter and adding 1/4 tsp. baking soda to coco powder if you don't have dutch process coco. These worked out well. Also, in lieu of parchment paper try a very light dusting of flour on a greased cookie sheet to prevent them from spreading to much. Mine came out perfect! To make them into a xmas cookie I lightly press a Hershey's peppermint kiss on top right out of the oven, they are pretty and delicious. Keeping them on the small side I got 90 cookies from 1 batch.

Man, these are awesome. I am not a chocolate lover at all, but we have some chocolate lovers in the family so I usually make one chocolate cookie for them. These are really good! They stayed soft and have a really nice complex flavor. I used Dutch cocoa and a little of a super dark cocoa I have, and only used 10 ozs. Of chocolate because that's all I had. I thought I screwed up because I forgot to put the butter in the first batch and had to beat it into the stiff dough at the end after I realized I had forgotten it and they still were perfect, same as the second batch I didn't screw up, so the recipe seems to be very forgiving. I also used king aurthurs espresso powder, which I put in anything chocolate. These cookies are great. I also rolled 1/2 of them in chopped pecans I had left from another cookie I made and that was great also.
I made the recipe as written BUT added a Trader Joe chocolate covered caramel wedge to each cookie (wrapped dough around the wedge before baking). Dear God. At least I only made a 1/2 batch.
Great recipe. Like many others I have augmented the recipe. My only addition was 1.5 tsp cayenne pepper. Other than that I followed to the letter.

My friend Lissa brought these to my AR Round Up in December 2015 and they were a hit. I am not a chocolate lover but these were wonderful and I had to make them. If you like brownies you will love these. I used Trader Joe's Pound Plus 72% Cacao Dark Chocolate. The dough is very thick, I used my #30 black scoop and got exactly 42 cookies. Perfect.

These cookies are very rich. They were completely devoured before the 10 minutes cooling were up. I didn't have Nescafe, so i used coffee flour from Trader Joe's, which turned out great and i think has better flavor than Nescafe. I also had to substitute chocolate chips for the Dutch chocolate. They have the richness of brownies, but consistency of cookies. I love browned butter in brownies so i may brown it first next time, and yes there will be a next time.

These taste like brownie cookies! So good! I was a little worried from reviews but glad I decided to make them anyway. I used cold butter instead of margarine and I think the cold helped keep them from spreading too flat like others had problems with. I will definitely be keeping this recipe! I used them as a base for my Pilgrim Hat cookies (top with Rollo's and mini Reece's cups and decorate with icing) for Thanksgiving - worked out perfectly! I did shape then into balls and smushed them into fat discs and baked them on parchment lined cookie sheet because the first sheet I did drop cookies didn't get round/flattened enough to use for my purposes.

These are great. I made them yesterday mainly for my boyfriend because he loves chocolate and they turned out really good and rich. I halfed the recipe since its only 2 of us. They were so gooey on the inside and nice and firm on the outside. We couldnt eat that many so I put the rest in a baggy. I ate one today and they are, in my opinion, even better! I made these with just cheap store brand cocoa and chocolate chips. I dont know why some people say you HAVE to make it with good quality chocolate because they turned out delicious with the cheap stuff. I guess its just your preference. I didnt have any problems with the dough at all and sat it in the fridge for 30 min to get more firm. They were very easy to roll in balls afterwards. This was an easy recipe and I will be making again!
very very good, i made them for my friends, and they loved them!! I halved the recipe, and it made a-TON so 5/5!!
It tastes like a brownie, but in cookie form. Melts in your mouth choclatey goodness.
Omg the best ever I added chocolate chips of course literally to die for I'm in heaven and I halfed the recipe cuz I have no will power
Nice soft cookies, real popular with the family. Only thing I did different was leave out the coffee.

I did not love the way these turned out especially when all of my family had to at least try it because I took the VERY time consuming way and I tried using cookie cutters, the batter for this is just not easy to work with. End result turned into very thin square cookies which they thought were brownies

This is the best fudgy chocolate cookie! So deep, dark chocolatey good. I used a 1.5 T. scoop, rolled them in my hands and they got so glossy. Then I used a cold drinking glass to slightly flatten them. They baked a perfect round cookie. But the first batch, I just scooped them on the baking sheet. The tops were crinkle-y and they were more mounded. I think I liked them best. Someone said they taste like a molten chocolate cake and I agree.
I love it
SUPER good! They don’t take much stuff to make, and only take ten minutes to bake.

These chocolate cookies were delicious just out of the oven, but hardened and lost their wonderful chocolate flavor when just a day old. It’s easy to overcook them. Pull them out of the oven when they still look undone.
